subject.title: Windows: lstat bottleneck causes 2-3x slower performance vs Mac (59% of CPU time)

question: Should OpenClaw accept operation-scoped realpath and existing-ancestor caches in plugin hook/skill and sandbox containment paths, or require a different Windows performance strategy?
rationale: The remaining implementation trades Windows filesystem performance against stale-path containment risk in security-sensitive code, which needs maintainer intent even though the issue is valid.

options.title: Accept scoped caches after PR blockers are fixed
options.body: Fix the open PR's build/proof blockers, rerun focused Windows and sandbox/plugin validation, then land the bounded operation-local cache design.

options.title: Reject containment-path caching
options.body: Keep the manifest-registry optimization and close or rewrite the linked PR so containment checks always re-read filesystem state per call.

options.title: Request a narrower replacement
options.body: Ask for a replacement PR that preserves only the cache scopes maintainers are comfortable owning and leaves the rest as documented performance debt.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped caches after PR blockers are fixed
recommendation.body: Fix the open PR's build/proof blockers, rerun focused Windows and sandbox/plugin validation, then land the bounded operation-local cache design.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked PR is assigned to vincentkoc and recent merged history shows ownership of the adjacent manifest-registry realpath cache fix.
